heroHeadline: UNSMIL Presses Halt to LAAF Executions as Libyan Coast Guard Intercepts Migrant Boat Before NGO Rescue
heroSubtitle: UNSMIL said Sep 16 it is "deeply concerned" by more than 30 executions carried out since Aug 23 by LAAF military courts in eastern Libya — the first use of capital punishment in the country since 2010 — and urged authorities to suspend further death sentences pending review; Amnesty International says at least 50 more people remain under sentence. On Sep 18, SOS Méditerranée said the Libyan Coast Guard intercepted a boat carrying roughly 80 migrants and returned them to Libya before its rescue ship Ocean Viking could reach it, part of a wider Mediterranean picture in which overall arrivals to Europe are down about 40% year-on-year but recorded deaths and disappearances have risen. Earlier in the period, Petroleum Facilities Guards blockaded Zawia refinery's main gate over pay (Sep 13) and a Benghazi House of Representatives session split over quorum disputes while advancing the '4+4' election committee's recommendations (Sep 14). No new military incidents or oil-infrastructure strikes were confirmed this period.
